definitions.explanation: Casual form of {端|はし} meaning 'edge' or 'end.' The っこ ending adds a familiar, slightly affectionate tone, often used in everyday conversation and with or by children.

examples.japanese: パンの{端|はし}っこが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I love the end pieces of the bread.

examples.japanese: {机|つくえ}の{端|はし}っこに{鍵|かぎ}を{置|お}いておいた。
examples.english: I left the key on the edge of the desk.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちはソファの{端|はし}っこに{座|すわ}って{絵本|えほん}を{読|よ}んでいた。
examples.english: The children were sitting at the edge of the sofa reading a picture book.

notes:
Casual variant of {端|はし} formed with the diminutive/familiar suffix っこ. It carries a friendlier, more concrete feel — useful in speech but generally not in formal writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {机|つくえ}の{端|はし}っこ: the edge of the desk
- パンの{端|はし}っこ: the end (heel) of a loaf of bread
- {端|はし}っこに{座|すわ}る: to sit at the edge
- {端|はし}っこを{切|き}る: to cut off the end

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {端|はし}: edge; end (neutral, all-purpose)
- {隅|すみ}: corner (interior corner of a room or space)
- {先|さき}: tip; point (the very end, often pointed)
